variants.headline: Builder signs for a new project
variants.sub: A construction contract for {project} has been awarded to {builder}.
variants.body:
The builder {builder} has signed a contract for {project} at an agreed price of {price}. The signature establishes an undertaking to build, not a completed building. Readers assessing {target} should distinguish the award from delivery, while taking seriously the obligations the agreement is meant to create.

An award defines a commercial undertaking, not earned revenue for all work or a finished asset for the client. Managers should distinguish contract value from execution. The agreed price is material, but it does not by itself settle the questions of performance that a building agreement necessarily leaves to delivery.

We take a critical view of {target}. A signature should not shelter inadequate stewardship, and responsible construction requires a more demanding standard than satisfaction that someone has agreed to undertake the work. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
